The era of retail users messing around with private keys themselves is basically coming to an end, and the demand for compliant custody may actually be pushed up by news like this.

Look, teacher—let’s explain RSI simply.

This is a momentum indicator: it tells you whether the move is strong or if it’s starting to get tired.

We use it to understand that if RSI is rising along with price, momentum is helping; but if price is rising while RSI is weakening, then watch out for divergence.

The biggest mistake: the biggest blunder is selling just because RSI is above 70, or buying just because it’s below 30. You must first look at the trend.

Quick example: if the coin is in an uptrend and RSI drops back from 50 and then rises again, that’s a stronger follow-through than randomly entering when RSI is at 30.

This time’s angle: wait for a clear confirmation instead of chasing the price.

RSI by itself isn’t enough. Link it with the trend, volume, support, and resistance—then your decision will be calmer and cleaner.

#baby $BABY Last night, with nothing to do, I went to the Babylon testnet to poke around and explore TBV’s chained gameplay built on top of Aave v4 and GoMining. When I first got started, it felt truly smooth: I staked 0.1 signet BTC into the dedicated vault, then smoothly borrowed 70% of the USDC to deploy for compute power. I finished the whole sequence in about three minutes. But once I calmed down and carefully worked through the underlying accounting logic of this system, I suddenly felt chills down my spine. @babylonlabs_io 

The easiest point for this strategy to blow up is that the settlement standards for liabilities and profits are completely out of sync. What we borrow from the lending platform is USDC (Aave’s variable rate is currently about 3.2%). But GoMining’s expected yield of 8% to 15% is paid out entirely in BTC.

This means you think you’re safely earning an interest-rate spread—when in reality you’re being forced to take on leverage and bet on the big pie’s up-or-down movement. If the market suddenly dumps, the BTC you mined will convert back to USD… and it probably won’t even be enough to cover the borrowed interest shortfall. What looked like a perfect arbitrage loop is already torn open by exchange-rate volatility.

Worse than a drop in coin price is the lag when withdrawing. Suppose you hit an extreme crash scenario—you can see price about to break the red line, and you urgently want to redeem the BTC to close the position. At this point, the claim delay becomes a death sentence: from when you submit the unlock request to when the assets actually arrive, it can be only a few hours, or it can drag on for two whole days.

On one side, there’s Aave’s ruthless real-time liquidation mechanism. On the other, Babylon’s forced time locks designed to prevent attacks. Players caught in the middle are extremely passive. Unless you have an additional stash of USDC on standby—ready to plug the hole at any moment—you’re basically left staring at the screen, watching your position get liquidated without mercy.

Let’s do the math: if you directly use USDC to buy GoMining’s Digital Miner, the whole process is far more straightforward—take the收益, no borrowing pressure, no fear of liquidation, and you don’t need to endure any withdrawal cooldown period at all.

TBV’s setup is indeed ingenious. It maximizes Bitcoin’s self-custody rights. But the double suffering it introduces after it stretches the timeline has already eaten away all that slim profit margin. This is more like an advanced game where institutional players use hedging tools—retail users, don’t rush to join the excitement. #eth $ETH

#baby $BABY 昨天夜里闲着没事，去 Babylon 测试网摸索了一把 TBV 叠加 Aave v4 与 GoMining 的连环玩法。刚上手时感觉确实丝滑：往专属金库里质押 0.1 个 signet BTC，顺利贷出 70% 的 USDC 拿去配置算力，一顿操作三分钟搞定。但当我静下心来仔细盘算这套逻辑的底层账本时，顿时觉得背脊发凉。@babylonlabs_io 

这个策略最容易翻车的地方，就是负债与利润的结算标准完全不在一个频道上。我们在借贷平台上贷出来的是 USDC（现在 Aave 的 variable rate 大约是 3.2%），可是 GoMining 预期给到那 8% 到 15% 的 expected yield，全是以 BTC 来发放的。

这就意味着，你以为自己在安稳地赚取利息差，实际上是被迫加杠杆在赌大饼的涨跌。要是赶上大盘跳水，你辛苦挖出来的币换算回美元，恐怕连填补借款利息的窟窿都够呛。这原本看似完美的套利闭环，早就被汇率波动撕开了一个大口子。

比币价下跌更折磨人的，是提币时的卡顿。假设遇到极端暴跌行情，眼看快跌破红线了，你急着想把大饼赎回来平仓。这时候 claim delay 就成了一道催命符——从你申请解锁到资产真正到账，短则几个钟头，长的话得干耗上整整两天。

一边是毫不留情的 Aave 实时清算程序，另一边是 Babylon 为了防范攻击而设立的强制时间锁。夹在中间的玩家极被动。除非你另外准备了一笔真金白银的 USDC 随时准备填坑救火，否则就只能死盯着屏幕，看着自己的仓位被无情强平。

算算账，如果直接掏 USDC 去买 GoMining 的 Digital Miner，流程要干脆得多：直接拿收益、无借贷压力、不怕被清算，压根不需要熬什么提现冷却期。

TBV 这套体系确实精妙，它最大程度捍卫了比特币的自我托管权。但它拉长战线后带来的双重折磨，早就把那点利润空间吃干抹净了。这属于机构玩家拿对冲工具玩的进阶游戏，散户真的别轻易凑热闹。#eth $ETH

#baby $BABY Yesterday at midnight I went to Babylon’s testnet to try out the TBV protocol—plus a new mining route that strings together Aave v4 and GoMining. The front-end flow really is smooth: deposit 0.1 signet BTC into the contract, then borrow USDC in a 70% ratio to set up mining power—done in three minutes. But once I dug into the underlying yield terms and did the math, I realized it isn’t that simple.@babylonlabs_io 

The biggest trap of this play is that the two sides of the deal are priced in completely different channels. The stablecoin you borrow from Aave is USDC (its current variable rate is around 3.2%), but the expected return you earn from GoMining—expected yield of roughly 8% to 15% annualized—is settled in BTC. On the surface, the spread looks like there’s money to be made; in essence, though, it’s effectively a leveraged bet on “the pie.” If the market pulls back sharply, the BTC you mine won’t even be enough to cover the interest shortfall once you convert it to dollars—the supposed arbitrage space on paper can be wiped out instantly by exchange-rate fluctuations.

Worse than the exchange-rate is the withdrawal mechanism and how it messes with your mindset. If BTC suddenly dumps through a spike and drives you close to the liquidation line, you’ll naturally want to pull out the BTC “pie” used as collateral to close the position. But because of the claim delay, unlocking your assets is fast only in hours—slow can take two days. On one side you have Aave’s unforgiving liquidation engine; on the other, Babylon’s hard time-lock rules for mainnet security. In extreme market conditions, if you don’t have USDC ready to top up beforehand, you’ll be forced to just watch as the system liquidates your orders at a bad price.

Compare that with the most straightforward alternative: just take USDC to buy GoMining’s Digital Miner—pay, get the computing power, and receive BTC. No need to carry the risk of liquidation from borrowing, and there’s no delay risk either. The intent behind the TBV combination is solid: it truly preserves Bitcoin’s self-custody. But it also pushes all the risks of interest-rate volatility and time costs onto the user.

This logic is currently better suited for institutions that have hedging tools; ordinary people can’t afford the stress. Take my advice: at least wait until fixed-rate products launch, lock the borrowing cost tightly, and then decide. Jumping in right now is simply paying for the system’s uncertainty with real money.#eth $ETH

The Fed won’t just be unable to cut rates—it may even reopen discussions about raising rates. Under this macro environment, not only altcoins—big BTC will likely suffer too. $VIC（VICUSDT） is staging a typical low-cap “hit-and-run” battle: a 72.731% gain over the past 24 hours, with the current price at 0.04814. Such a steep push looks more like liquidity-driven flashing rather than a fundamental repricing that has already happened. My clear view is: the bulls hold the high ground, but the supply line is too long; the risk of chasing is clearly higher than waiting for a pullback confirmation.

From a military perspective, price is the front line, while funding rates and open interest (OI) are logistics and troop deployment. The current funding rate is -0.00213327, indicating pronounced pressure from shorts paying; OI is at 95510054, meaning a large number of open contracts are piled up on the battlefield. Negative funding combined with a violent surge can easily lead to a short “encirclement”: if the price keeps charging higher, it can trigger stop-losses and liquidations for short positions, creating a second round of short squeeze; but extremely high OI also means leverage is crowded—if the main force withdraws, long liquidation cascades (a stampede) could happen just as quickly. Low-liquidity small-cap altcoin order books are thin, so you especially need to watch for wick spikes and chain liquidations.

At the macro level, market expectations for liquidity in risk assets determine whether the “ammunition” is sufficient; at the micro level, you should see whether after the rally OI keeps increasing or drops rapidly. Continued OI growth suggests new leverage is still entering and volatility may expand; a fast OI decline looks more like short covering, and the durability of the move is not necessarily strong. In terms of politics and global news, in a Trump-perspective view, statements on crypto policy, the degree of regulatory loosening/tightening, and overall risk appetite in markets can all affect capital rotation in altcoins—but you cannot treat political slogans as direct support for VIC’s long-term value. When political conflict or geopolitical risk heats up, capital typically first pulls back to tighten defenses; smaller coins are often under greater pressure than mainstream coins.

Emotions from KOLs on X can be treated as reconnaissance signals—not as a command to fire. If discussion suddenly becomes highly concentrated and everyone’s calls are extremely consistent, that’s exactly when you should guard against distribution after an emotional peak. Action-wise, I don’t recommend going heavily long here. If you already hold longs, take profit in batches and raise your stop-loss. If you’re in cash, wait for a contraction in volume and a pullback with OI cooling. If you want to short, you must wait until the squeeze momentum fades to avoid stubbornly fighting a trend in hard adversity. The core principle is simple: light position sizing, low leverage, preset stop-loss—first preserve your “troops,” then wait for the right moment.

#baby $BABY Recently, the Multi-Staking play has swept across the entire internet again. Put the BTC you have in hand up as underlying collateral across multiple networks, and ride the trend to harvest several layers of “wool.” The efficiency of capital circulation is indeed enviable. According to data from the Babylon official website as of August 4, more than 100,000 players have joined with funds, with a total locked amount of 56,853.16 BTC, which comes to roughly $5.64 billion.@babylonlabs_io 

The pot may be big, but from a retail investor’s perspective, watching the operation interface inevitably makes people uneasy: behind all this unbelievable wealth, exactly how many hidden risks are buried?

@babylonlabs_io  often hangs the phrase “single asset, multiple returns” on his tongue. The idea of stacked rewards sounds exciting, but people often ignore the fact that the risks are multiplying just as wildly—only they’ve been cleverly tucked into a lengthy instruction manual. There are several extremely opaque hard issues here:

Fee skimming and a liquidity illusion: The various nodes (FPs) usually first deduct a 3%–5% road fee. And the “interest” you receive is often a mix of different little coin types (such as #baby $BABY , etc.). If these reward coins can’t really make waves in the market and have no depth, then even the most enticing APY on the panel is just a string of empty numbers.

Penalties and joint responsibility: When funds are tied to multiple networks at the same time, if one node hits a problem that triggers a penalty, how much of the principal will be cut off? If you want to remove the staking of a certain chain halfway through, will it cause all other rewards to be invalidated as well?

The agony of the lock-up period: Nowadays, if you want to redeem your BTC, there are strict rules requiring you to wait for about 7 days. In this industry, seven days is enough to experience a full round of heavy drawdowns; in extreme market conditions you can only watch helplessly, with no chance to cut losses and run.

To put it plainly, it’s one thing for the project team to reach such an astonishing scale, but then to let retail investors flip through the whitepaper themselves, calculate allocations, and guess the limits—it’s honestly not very decent.

Whether multi-staking can truly break out isn’t about how many chains it can span. The key is that users must be given a clear, straightforward “staking statement” on the user side: node ownership, fee breakdown details, exactly how much actually ends up in their hands, the worst-loss floor, and how long it takes to exit. Only when all the cards are laid out on the table will everyone dare to press that confirmation button with confidence.#eth $ETH

If the market crashes one-sidedly, those seven days are enough to make you anxious—and you won’t be able to run even if you want to.

At the end of the day, with a project of this scale, it’s not really acceptable to make everyone dig through wordings and guess the rules themselves. For multi-staking to be adopted broadly, platforms must provide a “statement of accounts” that can be understood at a glance: which nodes belong to whom, the fee/take rate, how much net profit is earned, the worst possible loss, and how long it takes to withdraw. Why Basic Spot Trading is Permissible (Halal)Direct Ownership: 

You buy and take immediate possession of the actual asset (like a stock or cryptocurrency).No Leverage: You use only your own money, meaning no borrowed funds or debt.No Interest (Riba): Because no money is borrowed, you neither pay nor receive interest.

When Spot Trading Can Become Haram

Prohibited Assets: Buying shares in companies that deal in forbidden things like alcohol, pork, conventional banking, or adult entertainment.

Overnight Fees (Swaps): In forex spot trading, if a broker charges or pays an interest rate to hold a position overnight, it introduces riba.

Look, master—let’s explain Bollinger Bands in a simple way.

Bollinger Bands show whether the price has moved far from its average or is still within a normal range.
We use them to spot when price is compressed inside the bands, followed by a volume “explosion” that could lead to a solid move.

The biggest mistake: selling at the upper band in a strong uptrend. The price can ride the band for a long time.

Quick example: if the bands are tight and the price breaks with volume, we should watch the retest instead of rushing.

This time’s follow-up angle: wait for a clear confirmation instead of chasing the price.

Put simply, the IoT company Sequans isn’t playing with crypto anymore. They’ve just sold 344 BTC, and they still hold 314 more that are set to be cleared out. BTC is currently trading at $63,763.11, down 1.63% in the past 24 hours; ETH has also been hit, dropping to $1,867.45.

Honestly, this is pretty embarrassing. Sequans was originally in IoT chips. They used to envy others hoarding BTC for asset allocation, but once they see the volatility is too big to withstand, they quickly cut losses and return to their core business. Let’s do the math: 344 plus 314 equals 658 BTC in total. At the current price, that’s roughly a $41.95 million position. The first batch has already been smashed out; the remaining 314 BTC are like a sword hanging over everyone’s head—unknown when a concentrated sell-off will land another blow to the order book.

In the short term, this is simply a pure bearish signal. A publicly listed company openly announces, “I’m not playing anymore, and I’m continuing to dump,” and that kind of panic sentiment can spread to other retail traders and institutions. Especially those remaining 314 BTC—they could all dump into the market at any moment, adding another strike to an already weak market. On the funding side, it’s also a blood drain: once this batch is cleared, nearly $20 million in liquidity is withdrawn.

The medium-term impact is even more worrying. Sequans exiting isn’t an isolated case—it shows that the risk of traditional companies treating BTC as a strategic reserve is becoming exposed. If more companies that followed the trend and hoarded BTC can’t hold on and start imitating the liquidation, this chain reaction of sell pressure isn’t a joke.

My take is very clear: bearish in the short term—don’t rush to catch a falling knife. BTC at $63,763.11 probably can’t hold. Soon it will test the 60,000 psychological level. As long as those 314 BTC haven’t been fully sold off, any rebound is a chance for you to reduce exposure, not to act as a bag-holder. #baby $BABY Just now, I stared dead at the testnet data and finally got the funds anchored on-chain. I didn’t feel even a hint of satisfaction—instead, cold sweat kept pouring out. To run an extreme stress test for @babylonlabs_io , I went in hard: I intentionally used the same final deterministic provider (FP) private key to “stamp” two different blocks. Result: in less than three minutes, the locked assets were forcibly swept away—an exact 0.1% was extracted and sent to a black-hole address, and the remainder was then returned back to the account. No one came for manual review the entire time, and there was no need for any community vote. It was clean and ruthless, like a silent guillotine dropping.

That’s exactly what makes EOTS so terrifying. It strips humans of the right to interfere, turning any rule violation punishment into nothing but a fully automated arithmetic problem. As soon as you dare to touch this red line of double-signing, it’s the same as putting your safe’s password on a public billboard—any node on the network can just “take advantage” and execute the sanctions. The whole process follows a contingency trigger line pre-baked into your Taproot contract when you initially lock the funds. That underlying logic is cold-blooded: the only identification criterion is whether you can derive the private key by producing two conflicting proofs. If you meet the requirement, it immediately proceeds. Miners don’t care whether your server got hacked or the operator’s hands slipped—if there’s money to be made, they package it up and send it.

Compared with the staking deductions on the other side (Ethereum), this approach is more original and more decisive. Over there, when disasters strike—acts of God or human error at least you can argue and fight it out through DAO proposals; at worst, you can recruit nodes to do a hard fork to rescue things. But in Bitcoin’s mainnet system, destroyed funds are simply permanently erased from the UTXO ledger—no miracle-worker can save you. This rigid iron law creates extremely strong determinism; the price is absolute zero tolerance. Even if your operations machine gets compromised by hackers and triggers “passive violation,” the ruthless equation still won’t show even a drop of mercy—it carries out the execution as usual.

Taking the power of life-and-death judgment away from carbon-based beings and fully handing it over to silicon-based cryptography is the ultimate embodiment of the geek creed: refuse trust, accept only code. But along with that comes a total change in the survival rules for node operators. Previously, the goal was high availability; now it’s “one wrong move and the whole board is lost.” These rules are extremely reliable because they completely eliminate dependence on human nature. But they’re also terrifying because once the blade falls, you can’t even find a place to cry foul. #eth $ETH

#baby $BABY 刚才死死盯着测试网的数据最终上链，心里不仅没觉得高兴，反而直往外冒冷汗。为了给 @babylonlabs_io 做极限实测，我下了狠手，故意用同一个最终确定性提供者（FP）私钥对俩不同的区块盖了戳。结果不到三分钟，锁定的资产就被强制划走，精准抽取0.1%打入黑洞地址，余款才原路退回到账户。全程没谁来人工审核，也用不着社区投票，干脆利落得如同无声坠落的铡刀。

这恰好是 EOTS 最令人生畏的魅力所在。它剥夺了人类的干预权，把违规处罚彻底变成了纯自动化算术题。只要你敢碰双签这根红线，等同于把自家保险箱密码挂在公屏上，全网任意节点都能顺手牵羊来执行制裁。这套流程走的是你早期锁定资金时，预埋在 Taproot 合约里的备用触发线。那段底层逻辑冷酷无情，它唯一的辨识标准就是：能否通过两份冲突证明反推出私钥。只要达标立刻放行。矿工们才不管你是服务器被盗还是操作员手抖，有油水就直接打包。

相比隔壁以太坊的质押扣除，这玩法更原生态，也更决绝。那边遇到天灾人祸，起码能靠 DAO 提案扯皮，大不了拉拢节点来个硬分叉抢救一下。可是比特币这套主网系统里，被销毁的筹码就是真正在 UTXO 账本上灰飞烟灭，神仙难救。这种死板的铁律造就了极其强悍的确定性，代价则是绝对的零容错。哪怕运维机器遭遇黑客洗劫从而引发“被动违规”，冷酷的方程组也绝不讲半点情面，照常执刑。

把生死判决权从碳基生物手里收回，完全交接给硅基密码学，堪称极客信条的终极展现：拒绝信任，只认代码。但随之而来的，是节点维护者的生存法则彻底变了：以前追求高可用性，现在则是“一招不慎，满盘皆输”。这套规则极其靠谱，因为它彻底摒弃了对人性的依赖；但也极其骇人，因为当屠刀落下时，你连个喊冤的去处都找不到。#eth $ETH

What happened
To put it simply: crypto veterans have long agreed on one thing—“Not your keys, not your coins.” Everyone moves coins out of exchanges and into cold wallets, thinking that makes them absolutely safe. So what happened? The well-known hardware wallet Coldcard was exposed for a security vulnerability. Hackers exploited the flaw and laundered users’ funds, causing losses exceeding $83 million.

This isn’t a small incident. $83 million in real money has seemingly vanished. Coldcard used to brand itself as one of the safest Bitcoin cold-storage devices—until it got slapped hard in the face. This tells everyone: the money you thought was locked in a safe actually has a backdoor in the safe itself.

Why were they targeted? Because code audits of hardware wallet manufacturers have long been a black box. Hackers specifically look for vulnerabilities in these low-level firmware components to break in. With the amount involved now huge, the community is in an uproar.

Impact on the market
- Short term: Pure emotional blow. Retail traders see their own cold wallets are not safe—panic surges. - Medium term: It will force industry reshuffling. The adoption rate of multisig wallets will rise significantly. People will stop blindly trusting single-sig hardware cold wallets. This could be an opportunity for protocols focused on security infrastructure, but in the short term, the entire hardware wallet sector will face a trust crisis.

昨晚FNG指数直接砸到25，极度恐惧。周围所有人都在跑，社群里的情绪比菜市场还悲观。但我1987年开始做生意，见过太多次这种场景——最恐慌的时候，往往是聪明钱悄悄进场的时候。

第一，估值确实到位了。ETH从高点跌了63%，这个跌幅放在任何一个成熟市场，都已经是严重超跌的范畴。我经历过2015年、2018年的熊市，每次这种幅度的下跌，后面都跟着一波像样的反弹。不是说不会继续跌，但在这个位置继续看空，性价比已经很低了。

第二，成交量在放大。最近几天的成交量明显比之前活跃，说明有资金在承接。我不管别人怎么说，成交量骗不了人——如果真的是全面崩盘，应该是放量下跌，而不是这种缩量震荡。

第三，结构在筑底。1800这个位置很关键，是前期多次验证的支撑区间。ETH在这里稳住了，24小时涨了0.5%，虽然不大，但止跌信号已经出来了。

我的判断：未来7天，ETH会尝试向上突破。第一目标1920附近，止损放在1750，跌破就认错出场。

当然，我可能会看错。但在这个位置，我觉得值得押注。

Most investors focus on where they invest their money. Fewer think about where they invest their attention. Yet attention shapes decisions. What you read influences what you believe. What you repeatedly hear influences what you expect.

Thought for the Day. 
A distracted investor often makes emotional decisions. A focused investor is more likely to make disciplined ones.
Systems over emotion. Conviction over noise.

#baby  When reading the Babylon whitepaper, there’s a detail that’s especially worth taking a close look at. The official narrative repeatedly touts that when users lock BTC into on-chain vaults, that’s “self-custody.” They emphasize over and over that the assets never leave one layer of the network. But anyone who understands the “if you don’t hold the private key, it’s not really your coin” kind of hardcore principle will see that this story is dodging the real issue. Even if you do hold the “unboxing password,” this mechanism is no longer the same thing as the absolute sovereignty that those old-school believers hold dear. @babylonlabs_io 

The key trick is all in the position-building stage. The system effectively forces you to “sign off in advance” on a whole sequence of future actions. For example, once the oracle shows that BTC dumps and falls below 50,000, what should the liquidators do, how to force liquidation, how to freeze assets—you’ve already pre-signed. It’s like you have the only key to your house in your pocket, but you also handed someone a legally binding paper that lets them break in and move things around as soon as certain conditions are met. Even if these instructions haven’t been broadcast on-chain yet, in the underlying logic they’re already on standby. When the trigger moment finally arrives, the machine runs the program relentlessly—you basically can’t undo it. Ostensibly, the key belongs to you, but in extreme market conditions, the rights over the assets have long been handed over everywhere.

The harsher foreshadowing is buried in the governance token $BABY . A lot of people mistakenly think that those liquidation lines and challenge periods are immutable rules hard-coded into the base protocol. Too naive! These deadly variables are determined entirely by token holders with large stakes—those who control $BABY —through voting. That means the contract you agree with today can be overturned at any time by a proposal from a vested-interest faction. Back in the day, DAI’s old players already suffered this kind of silent setback: core parameters were suddenly changed, retail users’ collateral was liquidated instantly, and there wasn’t even a place to argue. The safety of your principal is, in effect, secretly tied to someone else’s voting power.

In short, at best, this is “delegated custody where you have to read people’s faces.” If you want to put idle BTC to work and earn yield, compromising with the rules is unavoidable—and yes, it may be safer than cross-chain bridges that get stolen. But we need to recognize reality and not let those flashy labels hypnotize you. Old rule: DYOR, figure out where the boundaries are and who has the power to change your rules. Your private key is in your own hands, yet you can’t stop the code—written to someone else’s script—from moving your BTC. So where exactly is the independence and autonomy? #eth $ETH

#baby $BABY For a long time, when people looked at PoS public blockchains, they always thought it was only natural that nodes could come and go freely. As long as the staking pool didn’t collapse, a different group of people could come in to package blocks and the network would keep running as usual. It wasn’t until I read the technical document @babylonlabs_io  in depth that I broke out in a cold sweat: if miners are replaced too quickly, it is actually digging a huge pit in the system’s long-term defense.@babylonlabs_io 

The fatal weakness here lies in the “residual power of the past.” When early large holders withdraw their funds and leave, they may take the money with them and no longer be subject to any punishment mechanism, but the signature credentials used to confirm blocks back then are still in their hands.

That gives bad actors a knife: they only need to spend a very low cost to buy up these discarded credentials on the market. Once they gather an absolute majority of the shares, they can secretly forge a parallel ledger record. At that point, the mainnet may appear flush with funds on the surface, but in reality the underlying defense has already been completely hollowed out by these “ghosts.”

To completely cut off the possibility of tampering with the past, Babylon has come up with a killer move: forcibly locking each node handover list into the state changes of Bitcoin’s UTXO network.

This is like taking an easily altered electronic roster and directly printing it into a stamped archive stored in the safest vault. With Bitcoin’s timestamp as backing, once the handover is complete, the predecessor’s cryptographic credentials instantly become waste paper. Want to overturn it? Only if they can hack the world’s largest computing power network.

Of course, there is no free lunch in the world. Clinging to this super thigh comes at the cost of giving up some independent operational space.

What used to be a handover that could be confirmed in seconds now has to honestly queue up and wait for Bitcoin’s slow block confirmations. If the mainnet becomes seriously congested, its own operating rhythm will inevitably be slowed down. For sectors that require frequent interactions, this layer of armor can seem somewhat heavy. How to find the best balance between absolute tamper-resistance and native agility is definitely the hardcore challenge that $BABY  and the entire Babylon ecosystem must face next.#eth $ETH

Japan and the U.S. Team Up to Intervene in the Yen! BTC $63,538 Faces Risk of Forced Liquidation Pressure from Carry Trades

💡 Bearish📉: Fears of carry trade unwinds triggered by joint U.S.-Japan intervention in the yen are weighing on BTC in the short term.

In plain terms, the two central banks of the U.S. and Japan did something big together: they both stepped in to buy the yen. The yen had been falling all the way to 163.73 per $1; Japan’s central bank got frustrated and directly “dumped” about $36.6 billion in support. The U.S. then also stepped in to help—how much it actually put in was not disclosed. On the surface, this looks like a foreign-exchange market issue, but it has a lot to do with the crypto world. In recent years, the yen has been cheap. A bunch of institutions borrowed low-interest yen to buy high-risk assets worldwide—such as U.S. stocks and Bitcoin. This is called a carry trade. Now, with the U.S. and Japan working together to push the yen higher, borrowing costs are skyrocketing. Funds that previously added leverage will have to quickly close positions and repay. The first to be sold off—because it’s extremely liquid—is BTC.

In the short term, BTC is already pulling back. Over the past 24 hours, it’s down slightly 1.18% to $63,538.31. Market panic isn’t really about the number $36.6 billion itself; it’s about the signal that the U.S. Treasury—rarely—participated in intervention. It indicates top-level authorities are highly alert to leverage risk in the financial system. Once a carry-trade liquidation wave kicks off, hedge funds will sell their crypto assets without hesitation just to save themselves. Since ETH has slightly weaker liquidity, it’s also down 0.36% to $1,857.77, and clearly money is withdrawing.

For the medium term, this kind of cross-border coordinated intervention often breaks the market’s existing liquidity expectations. If the yen continues to appreciate, the bubble in global high-yield assets will be steadily squeezed. As the “cheap yen” big liquidity faucet gets tightened, it will be difficult to see substantial incremental capital pouring into the crypto market in the short run. Overall price action will likely continue to face downward pressure.

To be honest, I’m clearly bearish on this move. Guys, don’t rush to catch falling knives now—any rebound is a chance for you to reduce exposure. 💡 Bad-news bombshell: Hardware wallet credibility has been shaken, market panic is heating up, and funds may withdraw even faster.

The stolen amount jumped from $30M to $116M directly—four waves of back-to-back attacks in four days. Coinkite even said these past few days are the darkest moments in the company’s history. In plain terms, this hack was carried out by repeatedly robbing the wallet’s private keys. They thought $30M would be the end of it, but in under a week it nearly quadrupled—how much is left on the books depends entirely on the hacker’s mood.

In the short term, panic is absolutely going to hammer the market. Hardware wallets were supposed to be the last safety line in crypto. Now that the line has been breached, retail investors’ first reaction is to flee. BTC has just climbed to $63,550; ETH is struggling around $1,855.44. This trust crisis will likely cause in-market hedging/defensive capital to pull out faster.

The medium term is even worse: regulators will most likely step in to target hardware wallets with oversight, compliance costs will skyrocket, and the industry’s profit margins will be squeezed.

【Data doesn’t lie, but most people can’t understand it】

Today is $ 1862.76. A week ago it was almost at the same spot. Over the 7 days it moved by about 0.6%. A month ago? It was roughly hovering around $ 1880.

Doesn’t that sound boring? But the devil is in the details.

The market fear and greed index (FNG) is now 25.

What does 25 mean? It falls into the “extreme fear” category. According to the textbook version, this is when retail investors should be fleeing and selling at a loss, right?

But ETH didn’t keep getting smashed. Instead, it held steady.

The weekly average is 27. Historically, this kind of combination has happened many times—when FNG drops to a trough, the price often begins to form a bottom.

I first noticed this pattern back in 2019. Back then, the whole market was in despair. The people who bought the dip later ended up making money—not because of luck, but because on-chain data told me: when retail investors panic-sell, large players are quietly taking the other side.

So the question is—

**What does this fact actually imply?**

It suggests that there may be a group of people using other people’s fear to set up their own positions—not through “calling trades,” but through logic. On-chain data shows that exchange net inflows are declining and the number of large-holder addresses is quietly increasing. These signals show up days earlier than the candlestick chart.

Who will be affected?

Short-term traders will find it painful, because a choppy bottoming process drains patience. But for anyone looking at a horizon of six months or more, this is actually worth keeping an eye on.

Does the business logic hold?

I tend to think it does. Big institutions can’t possibly be taking positions at high levels when FNG is at 80. What they want is room to build positions. The more panicked the market is, the more favorable it is for them.

Now it just comes down to whether this time can truly succeed in forming a bottom.

Can this actually play out in real life? Or do you have other signals on your side? #ETH #加密分析 #QUID #Market Insights

【数据不说谎，但大多数人听不懂】

今天$ 1862.76，一周前差不多还是这个位置，7日下来个0.6%，一个月前？大概在$ 1880左右晃悠。听起来是不是很无聊？但魔鬼藏在细节里。

市场恐慌指数FNG现在25。

25是什么概念？属于极度恐惧那一档。按教科书说法，这时候应该散户在割肉跑路，对吧？

但ETH没有继续砸，反而稳住了。周均值27，历史上这种组合出现过很多次——FNG跌到谷底，价格反而开始筑底。

我第一次注意到这个规律是在2019年。当时也是市场一片哀嚎，结果那波抄底的后来都赚了。不是因为运气，是因为链上数据告诉我：散户恐慌抛售的时候，大户在悄悄接。

那问题来了——

**这件事实处意味着什么？**

意味着可能有一批人正在用别人的恐惧给自己布局。不是喊单，是逻辑。链上数据能看到交易所净流入在降，大户地址数在悄悄增加，这些信号比K线早那么几天。

谁会受影响？

短线操作的人会很痛苦，因为震荡磨底最消磨耐心。但对于看半年以上的人，这种时候反而值得盯着。

商业逻辑通不通？

我倾向于认为通。大机构不可能在FNG 80的时候高位接盘，他们要的是建仓空间。市场越恐慌，对他们越有利。

#baby $BABY Talking about Babylon and this setup, its underlying architecture design really is impressive. The headline feature is to let large $BTC holders avoid cross-chain transfers and zero custody, keeping the coins in their own hands to capture the upside directly. But while this tempting “delicacy” looks so enticing, it’s riddled with plenty of glass shards. For insiders who are closely watching $BABY  and the big-bread ecosystem, it’s time to drop the rose-colored glasses and see its real soft underbelly. @babylonlabs_io 

First, look at the hidden hazards in the consensus layer. The security firm Zellic has already dug into the details of this mechanism: it’s too dependent on the honesty of external data relayers. Once the mainnet goes down, as long as a malicious mining pool moves in during the window when nodes are restarting—sending out a forged fork ledger—it can trick light clients and leave them “bullied.” Even more outrageous is the underlying signature algorithm: it was found to have a timing discrepancy flaw. If things get ugly, attackers could trace back through it and potentially compromise your private keys. The codebase previously also had a strange incident: people who cashed out early and already emptied their assets still managed to stay attached to the system and collect distributions anyway. This ledger defense is riddled with loopholes.

The development team’s basic competence is also hard to watch. The block-production tempo across the two chains was never really in sync. As a result, when handling cross-chain data, they used an extremely arbitrary, disorderly code logic. That meant the results computed by different mining rigs were all over the place; in the end, the chain couldn’t reconcile the ledger, causing it to simply freeze and come to a halt.

But the most fatal issue is the real financial hemorrhage caused by congestion. Go back and look at that Cap-1 live event in August 2024: the quota limit was clearly only 1000 BTC, yet the incoming 21,000 individual orders still stuffed all 6 blocks full. In those days, transfer fees were violently boosted from a mere $0.5 up to $132! It happened because the project team wrote the refund fee rate as hard-coded dead logic—so just the act of withdrawing capital consumed and疯狂吞噬ed a whopping 45% of the Gas expenditure of the entire Bitcoin network at the time.

Putting the project’s entire survival and lifeline on the mood of the big-bread mempool is like walking a tightrope blindfolded. If they can’t fix these rigid fee-rate and “code dead spot” vulnerabilities, then when the next fee war erupts, the real question is whether it can even hold up and survive. $ETH #eth

◇What is Ethereum (ETH)?

■ ​If Bitcoin is digital gold, Ethereum is the decentralized supercomputer powering the internet.

●​Launched in 2015 by Vitalik Buterin, Ethereum is the second-largest cryptocurrency by market cap. Unlike traditional digital currencies, its primary goal is to run smart contracts—self-executing code that operates automatically without banks, lawyers, or central authorities. 
 
■​ Key Takeaways:

●​ETH (Ether): The native token used to pay network transaction fees (called "gas").  
​Ecosystem Engine: It powers DeFi (decentralized finance), NFTs, decentralized gaming, and Web3 applications.  
●​Proof-of-Stake: Uses an energy-efficient consensus mechanism where users stake ETH to secure the network and earn rewards.  

■​ In short: ETH isn't just a currency—it’s the foundational fuel for the decentralized Web3 economy.

Every major geopolitical event creates two types of traders:

❌ Those who react to headlines.

✅ Those who follow the money.

Instead of asking “Should I buy BTC now?”, ask “Where is capital flowing?”

🛢️ 1. Oil — The First Signal

If tensions escalate, oil prices often rise due to concerns about supply disruptions.

Higher oil prices can fuel inflation worries, making investors more cautious about risk assets like crypto.

🥇 2. Gold — The Fear Gauge

When uncertainty increases, investors often move toward gold.

If gold continues climbing while stocks and crypto struggle, it usually reflects a risk-off environment.

₿ 3. Crypto — Watch the Leaders

Don’t just watch prices.

Watch how they react.

📌 $BTC holding key support despite negative news can be a sign of resilience.

📌 $ETH often reflects broader market confidence once buyers return.

📌 $BNB is worth monitoring as one of the market’s largest exchange ecosystem tokens.

If tokenized gold assets such as PAG or XAUT gain attention while BTC weakens, it may suggest investors are seeking safety rather than taking on additional risk.

Two Possible Scenarios

📈 If diplomacy progresses:

• Oil may cool.
• Market sentiment could improve.
• BTC , ETH , and other quality cryptocurrencies may benefit if investors become more comfortable taking risk again.

📉 If tensions escalate:

• Oil could rise further.
• Gold may continue attracting safe-haven demand.
• Crypto volatility may increase, especially for smaller altcoins.

I’m not trying to predict the future.

The market rewards preparation—not prediction.

ETH 今天慢慢磨上来了，价格重新回到 1875 附近，但先别急着追。

结论是：ETH 短线偏多，先小幅回踩，再去测试 1950。1850 守住以前，回调先按蓄力看；1950 没有真正站稳以前，也别把区间反弹当成主升浪。

ETH 现在约 1876，过去 24 小时最低 1838，最高 1882。

为什么这么判断？

1）Daan Crypto Trades（@DaanCrypto）今天把 ETH 的核心区间定在 1850—1950。他认为突破 1950 才能进一步看 2100，跌破 1850 则要防 1750。现在价格重新回到 1850 上方，短线仍有继续测试区间上沿的条件。

2）Michaël van de Poppe（@CryptoMichNL）今天认为 ETH/BTC 仍处在上升趋势，回调更适合观察承接。他早些时候还给出 1800 需要守住、突破 2000 后看 2300 的判断。现在 ETH/BTC 约 0.02934，说明 ETH 相对 BTC 仍偏强，但 0.03 附近还会有压力。

3）Cheds（@BigCheds）的 ETH 三日图把 1820—1860 标成关键支撑区域。结合实时 K 线，ETH 已重新站上 4 小时 EMA20（约 1868），正在测试 EMA50（约 1877）；只要回踩不丢 1850，这一轮修复就还没有走完。

把这些观点和实时 K 线合在一起，接下来只看一条路线：

ETH 从 1875 附近先回踩 1865—1850，预计在这里获得承接，随后继续反弹，先看 1900，再看 1950。到 1950 附近先看卖压，不追高。

所以方向很明确：先回踩，后上涨；1850 守住就看 1950。

这条路线的失效条件只有一个：ETH 4 小时收盘跌破 1850，反弹又收不回来。出现这个信号，短线偏多判断取消，下一步先看 1800，极端一点看 1750。

如果做区间或者网格，可以观察 1850—1950；但 1850 确认失守后，就不要再拿震荡逻辑硬扛单边下跌。

以上是行情路径推演，不是稳赚信号。

你觉得 ETH 这次能不能真正站上 1950？

Texas Governor Halts Power Grid Approval for Data Centers! BTC $63,948 Miners Dodged a Bullet

💡 Impact Assessment: Neutral to Slightly Bullish. Signed contracts are unaffected; short-term panic about a selloff is cleared.

In one sentence
Texas Governor has paused power grid data center approvals, but contracts already approved for mining companies are not affected—just a false alarm.

What’s going on
Put simply, this week Texas Governor Greg Abbott pulled a move: he announced a pause on data center approvals tied to the power grid operator ERCOT, pending an audit. The moment the news hit, many miners felt a jolt. After all, Texas is a major base for crypto mining in North America—if power were truly cut, capacity would have to be slashed significantly.

But hold on, folks—Bernstein quickly poured cold water on it, or more accurately, offered a steadying reassurance. They noted that this pause applies only to new applications. Power contracts for mining companies that were already signed in black and white are unaffected. If you want new land to expand capacity, you’ll have to wait for the moment. But existing production capacity is rock solid; the fundamentals aren’t broken.

Market impact
In the short term, this is basically an emotional “fake drop” washout. Funds that piled in at the first rumor find they misread the situation and then have to come back to cover positions. As the news was digesting, it’s actually a sign that the near-term bearish pressure has run its course. BTC is trading at $63,948, and has already rebounded nearly 2% intraday. That suggests panic capital has largely been absorbed. ETH is moving in sync too: up 1.85% intraday to $1,877.58.

From a mid-term perspective, this audit could even benefit industry compliance and consolidation. Texas grid authorities will “settle accounts,” cleaning up those non-compliant, under-the-table small miners that secretly exceed power quotas. Large compliant players—Riot, Marathon, and others—would be positioned to capture a larger share of the market. Institutional capital loves the logic of higher concentration; a “selloff” is not really on the table.

My take
Honestly, I’m bullish here and not looking to short. BTC is holding around $63,948. Since the biggest policy landmine has been proven to be a dud, there’s little to fear. For the short term, the target is to break above the previous high. As long as this sentiment holds, dips are likely to become buy opportunities. ETH at $1,877.58 will get a “share of the soup” along with the broader market. Those shorts betting on miners panicking and dumping to drive a selloff are probably about to get a lesson. The data and the chart are both pretty clear—go with the trend and go long.

我的判断
讲真，这位置我看多不做空。现在BTC守在$63,948，既然最大的政策地雷被证明是哑炮，那就没啥好怕的。短期目标先看突破前高，只要这波情绪能延续，回踩就是上车机会。ETH在$1,877.58跟着大盘喝汤。那些指望矿工恐慌性抛售砸盘的空头，估计要被教训了。数据和盘面都挺明确，顺势做多就完事了。

Entered the crypto game with #ETH 5 yuan, and now I support my whole family by trading and flipping coins. I’ve stepped on every pitfall there is, and I’ve also summed up the most practical trading rules. If your funds are within 500,000, read these lessons carefully—at least you can avoid ten years of detours.

Trend reversals never happen quietly. In a downtrend, if three bullish candles suddenly pop up, or in an uptrend the pullback doesn’t exceed three consecutive bearish candles, that’s the market giving you a wink. I’ve used this signal to dodge countless crashes and seize plenty of reversal opportunities.

A ranging or choppy market tests your patience the most, but before a breakout there are always clues. Volume quietly increases while price stays flat—that’s the main force building energy. Remember: wait until two bullish volume bars cover the bearish volume bars, then act—don’t rush in as the vanguard.

The art of holding coins lies in "waiting like an idiot." In a strong market, as long as the daily chart doesn’t break below the moving average, no matter how dull or lagging the indicators become, just hold. I’ve seen too many people jump off early because of an oversold signal—then they missed the following 3x rally. That kind of regret is brutal!

Candlestick patterns speak for themselves. A bullish candle paired with two doji stars is like taking a deep breath midway through a run: rest, then charge again. Every time I see this formation, I get excited—because it often means the main force never planned to stop.

The market loves to slap consensus in the face. When everyone is chanting "this time is different," you should be on guard. Before last year’s big crash, all kinds of groups were showing off their long positions on contracts. I cleared out my holdings back then and was mocked. Then what happened?

When the KDJ J-line drops below -12, it’s like a spring compressed to the bottom. But don’t rush to bottom-fish—wait for the rebound to confirm before you move. This trick has helped me catch countless short-term opportunities, especially for futures traders.

At breakout time, volume around 8% is the healthiest. Too big means the chips are loosening, too small means it’s a fake breakout. This is something I only understood after paying tens of thousands of yuan in tuition—now I’m telling you for free.

After years of struggling in the crypto market, I understand best the anxiety and confusion retail traders feel. If you’re looking for a direction, feel free to look through my analysis more. On this investment path, sometimes getting the right people matters more than getting the right market timing. Remember: controlling risk is always more important than chasing huge profits. Survive first, and then you’ll be able to wait for the opportunity that belongs to you!

I’m Yuge—helping you stay unlost on your crypto journey. If you want to avoid traps, trade steadily and follow the rhythm so you can profit.

#ETH 5万元入圈，到如今靠炒币养活全家，我踩过所有该踩的坑，也总结出最实用的交易铁律。如果你资金在50万以内，认真看完这些心得，至少能让你少走十年弯路。

趋势反转从来不会悄无声息。当下跌趋势里突然蹦出三根阳线，或是上涨中的回调不超过三连阴，这就是市场在给你递眼色了。我靠这个信号躲过无数次暴跌，也抓住不少反转机会。

震荡行情最考验耐心，但突破前总有迹可循。量能悄悄放大却价格横盘，这就是主力在蓄力。记住，等两次阳量盖过阴量再动手，别急着当冲锋队。
持币的艺术在于"傻等"。强势行情里，只要日线不破均线，管它指标怎么钝化。我见过太多人因为一个超卖信号就提前下车，结果错过后面三倍涨幅，那叫一个悔啊！

K线组合会说话。中阳线配两根十字星，就像跑步中途的深呼吸，歇完接着冲。这种形态我见了就兴奋，往往意味着主力根本没打算停。
市场最爱打脸共识。当所有人喊着"这次不一样"的时候，你就该警惕了。去年那波暴跌前，各个群都在晒合约多单，我当时清仓还被嘲笑，结果呢？

KDJ的J线跌到-12以下，就像弹簧压到底。但别急着抄底，等它反弹确认再动手。这个技巧帮我抓住无数短线机会，特别适合合约玩家。
突破时的量能8%左右最健康，太大说明筹码松动，太小则是假突破。这是我交了几十万学费才悟透的，现在免费告诉你。

在币圈摸爬滚打这些年，最懂散户的焦虑和迷茫。如果你正在找方向，不妨多来看看我的分析。投资这条路，有时候跟对人，比看对行情更重要。记住，控制风险永远比追求暴利关键，活下来才能等到属于你的大机会！

#ETH A few years ago, I really thought trading crypto had some real method to it—stuff like candlestick charts, Chan theory, indicator crossovers—you even had to stare at the screen day and night. It felt like if you could “understand” those twisty lines, you could make money. 
Until I went on a full three disastrous blowups. I was completely done. Alright, I won’t study anything anymore—I’m just going full “lay flat.” I’ll try the most “stupid” method that’s accepted in the crypto community. 
Turns out, just by laying flat like that, my account actually grew from 1,500U to 210,000U. Then I could finally achieve my first million in life. I was flying with joy. 
The method is so simple you might not believe it—it’s just three rules: 
First, only buy breakouts—never touch the range-bound action. 
No games with washouts, fake moves to bait people, or consolidation. I don’t even look. If the price suddenly smashes through a new high, I jump in immediately. If it’s a real breakout, I follow the trend. If it’s a fake breakout, I cut the loss and run right away. This thing doesn’t rely on guessing—it’s all about whether you’re willing to act and whether you can pull the trigger decisively and exit in time. 
Second, never go heavy. Don’t even think about it—use a 20% position size. 
Every time, invest a little bit of money. If you make a profit, you quickly stash it away—you never chase greed. If you get unlucky and get stopped out, then take a rest. Don’t add positions, don’t stubbornly hold, and don’t do the opposite. 
While other people try to place a dozen trades a day, running around like their feet never touch the ground, I only do one or two trades a week—and I end up making more. 
Third, only trade the trend you can actually understand. 
Don’t bottom-fish. Don’t guess tops. And don’t obsess over what the future will look like. Just follow the big direction. When it goes up, you buy by chasing. When it falls, you sell by keeping pace. Eat your meals the trend way. 
A lot of people mock me, saying I “can’t draw lines” and “can’t analyze.” 
Laughable. They’re still sitting there “drawing the future” on their candlestick charts, while my account has already skyrocketed to 210,000U. 
It’s not that I’m that awesome—it’s that I finally stopped messing around blindly. 
If you really want your account to grow by multiples, stop studying all those mystical trading setups. Apply the “dumbest” method to the extreme—that’s real intelligence. 
What you’re missing isn’t some high-level technical skill—it’s execution that can actually make your account grow. 
Don’t just watch—try following it for 30 days. The results will definitely surprise you more than you can imagine! #合约养家

#ETH 前几年我真觉得炒币得有门道，什么 K 线、缠论、指标交叉，还得没日没夜盯着盘，好像看懂那些弯弯曲曲的线就能赚钱似的。​
直到爆亏三次，我彻底麻了。得了，啥也不研究了，摆烂！就用币圈公认最 “笨” 的法子试试。​
没想到啊，就这么一躺平，账户居然从 1500U 涨到了 21万 U。​那会实现人生中第一个100万，开心到飞起、
方法简单到你可能不信，就三条：​
第一，只买突破，不碰震荡。​
什么洗盘、诱多、盘整，我瞅都不瞅。只要价格哐当一下冲破新高，我直接就上！真突破了就跟着趋势走，假突破了赶紧止损跑路。这玩意儿不靠猜，就看你敢不敢下手、能不能果断撤。​
第二，重仓？想都别想！就用 20% 仓位。​
每次就投点小钱，赚了就赶紧揣兜里，绝不贪多。要是运气差被止损了，就歇着，不加仓、不硬扛、不反过来操作！别人一天恨不得做十几单，忙得脚不沾地，我一周也就一两单，反倒赚得更多。​
第三，只做自己看得懂的趋势。​
不抄底、不猜顶、不瞎琢磨未来啥样。就跟着大方向走，涨就追着买，跌就跟着卖，顺着趋势混口饭吃呗。​
好多人笑话我，说我 “不会画线”“不会分析”。​
可笑死我了，他们现在还在那儿对着 K 线 “画未来” 呢，我账户都飙到21万 U 了。​
不是我多牛，是我终于不瞎折腾了。​
你要是真想把账户翻几番，别再研究那些玄乎的战法了。把最笨的方法用到极致，那才是真聪明。​
你缺的不是啥高深技术，是能让账户涨起来的执行力。​
别光看着，真照着做 30 天试试，结果绝对超乎你想象！#合约养家

title: Bessent Suggests US-Iran Hormuz Deal Possible in Coming Days
subTitle:
$BTC $XAU $CL 
Global markets are closely watching the Middle East after U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent suggested that a diplomatic agreement involving the United States, Iran, and the Strait of Hormuz could be reached within the coming days.
The remarks have fueled optimism that recent mediation efforts—led by regional partners including Qatar—may be producing meaningful progress. While no final agreement has been announced, discussions are reportedly focused on reducing regional tensions, improving maritime security, and ensuring the continued flow of global energy supplies.
Why the Strait of Hormuz Matters
The Strait of Hormuz is one of the world's most important shipping routes, with a significant share of global crude oil and liquefied natural gas passing through the narrow waterway every day. Any disruption can quickly impact energy prices, inflation, and overall investor sentiment.
A successful diplomatic agreement would help lower geopolitical risks, stabilize shipping operations, and reduce uncertainty across global financial markets.
Market Reaction
Oil traders are monitoring developments closely, as easing tensions could reduce the geopolitical risk premium currently reflected in crude prices. Meanwhile, equity and cryptocurrency investors are also paying attention, since improving geopolitical conditions often encourage demand for risk assets.
Bitcoin and the broader crypto market could benefit if investors gain confidence from a decline in global uncertainty. However, markets are likely to remain volatile until an official agreement is confirmed.
What Investors Should Watch
Official statements from the U.S., Iran, and Qatar.Updates regarding the reopening and security of the Strait of Hormuz.Oil price movements and global market sentiment.Bitcoin's reaction as geopolitical headlines continue to influence risk appetite.
Scott Bessent's comments have increased expectations that a breakthrough may be approaching. Although negotiations are still ongoing and no agreement has been finalized, even the prospect of a diplomatic solution has become an important catalyst for global markets.
If a deal is reached in the coming days, it could mark a significant step toward regional stability while providing support for stocks, cryptocurrencies, and energy markets.

translatedData.content:
Yesterday I reran Babylon’s Peg-In transaction construction flow. I originally thought its pre-signed transactions only handled the usual Timelock, but when I unpacked the Raw Transaction and traced down to the specific HTLC output script path, I immediately found an underlying risk that everyone seems to have overlooked.
In the marketing, they talk about trustless self-custody, but when you get down to how the pre-signed transaction is actually constructed, it depends on a preceding Pre-PegIn HTLC output. I captured the concrete data flow: before the staking transaction is broadcast to the chain, the staker’s client must offline hard-sign a pre-constructed HTLC spending path.
This script splits into two core branches: one is the single-sign path after 64,000 blocks for the normal unbonding flow; the other is the slashing condition pre-bound via a pre-signed HTLC. The issue lies precisely in the off-chain interaction of this HTLC path. Because BTC lacks native opcodes, this HTLC transaction’s Hash Preimage and the covenant committee’s verification signatures are required to be assembled and pre-signed at the exact moment the staker initiates staking—within the local client.
This exposes an extremely hardcore operational pitfall: most retail users rely on the frontend SDK to automatically construct this complex HTLC Raw Tx. If, when generating the HTLC pre-signed transaction, the frontend makes even minor scaffolding-level tweaks to the burn-address or timeout-return HTLC logic, then in your wallet you’ll only see Taproot addresses in a standard P2TR format—you won’t be able to decode the Raw Hex byte-by-byte to verify it.
@babylonlabs_io  Choosing to combine Pre-PegIn with HTLC to fill in BTC’s script limitations is technically very sound. But after I personally unpacked this script, the only three hands-on indicators I’ll look at next are:
- A byte-level audit comparing the open-source code of the pre-signing construction client on GitHub.
- Under heavy Mempool congestion, the on-chain response latency when this pre-signed HTLC transaction gets stuck due to insufficient RBF fees.#baby $BABY #ETH 
- The online rate of the covenant committee nodes when verifying HTLC preimages at high speed.
Having the HTLC logic in the code “works” is one thing, but whether the blind-signed Pre-PegIn transactions can execute smoothly in a real, highly congested BTC mainnet environment is another.

content:
我昨天重新跑了一遍 Babylon 的 Peg-In 交易构造流程，本来以为它的 pre-signed交易只是处理常规的 Timelock，结果把 Raw Transaction 解包拿到具体的 HTLC Output 脚本路径时，当场发现了一个被大家忽略的底层风险。
宣传里都在讲无桥自托管，但具体到 pre-signed 交易的构建时，它其实依赖一个前置的 Pre-PegIn HTLC 输出。我抓了具体的数据流，在质押交易广播上链之前，Staker 的客户端就必须在链下硬性签好一笔预构造的 HTLC 支出路径。
这套脚本拆成了两个核心分支：一条是满 64000 区块后走常规 Unbonding 的单签路径，另一条就是通过 Pre-signed HTLC 预先绑定的 Slashing 条件。问题恰恰出在这条 HTLC 路径的链下交互上。因为 BTC 缺少原生算子，这笔 HTLC 交易里的 Hash Preimage和 Covenant 委员会的验证签名，是要求在 Staker 发起质押的瞬间，就在本地客户端完成组装和预签名的。
这暴露出极其硬核的实操隐患：散户基本都是靠前端 SDK 自动调用去构造这段复杂的 HTLC Raw Tx。如果前端在生成 HTLC Pre-signed 交易时，对 Burn 地址或者超时退回的 HTLC 逻辑做了一点脚手架层面的微调，你在钱包里看 Taproot 地址全是常规的 P2TR 格式，根本没法逐字节解码 Raw Hex 去校验。
@babylonlabs_io 选择用 Pre-PegIn 结合 HTLC 来补足 BTC 的脚本限制，技术逻辑确实很顺。但我亲自动手解包完这段脚本后，接下来我只会看三项实操指标：
预签名构造客户端在 GitHub 上的开源代码与字节级审计对比。
当 Mempool 高压拥堵时，这笔 Pre-signed HTLC 交易因为 RBF 费用不足被卡住的链上响应延迟。#baby $BABY #ETH 
Covenant 委员会在极速验证 HTLC Preimage 时的节点在线率。
代码里的 HTLC 逻辑跑得通是一回事，但在真实的 BTC 主网高拥堵环境里，盲签出来的 Pre-PegIn 交易能不能毫无摩擦地执行，是另一回事。

translatedData.content:
Last night in the group chat I saw a few old-timers抢 Babylon (BABY) for the second Cap. They set the fee to 150 sat/vB just to push BTC into the contract. Everyone keeps saying “native self-custody,” with zero cross-chain risk—like if you don’t take the BTC out, the yield is basically free.
But many people haven’t even looked up the hard requirements in the BabylonGenesis parameters. BTC unbonding must go through a Taproot transaction script called an Unbonding Output. The official documentation spells it out clearly: this Unbonding Output forcibly locks to a Timelock covering 1,008 Bitcoin blocks (a full 7 days), and it also embeds the multi-sig threshold for the Covenant committee.

On the surface, people think, “7-day lockup is pretty short; Ethereum unbonding also has to queue.” However, applying the logic of Ethereum DeFi to Babylon is a fatal cognitive mismatch. On Ethereum or a standard Cosmos PoS chain, your Unbonding process is executed by smart contracts. If an extreme black-swan event happens in the middle, the derivative protocol can still find secondary liquidity on a DEX to realize value at a discount.

But Babylon relies purely on Bitcoin UTXO primitives. When you initiate an early unbonding, your UTXO changes from a Staking Output to an Unbonding Output. In this dead window of 1,008 blocks, the BTC is in an awkward state on-chain: it can’t continue earning PoS-chain yield settlements, and it also can’t be re-staked by any on-chain protocol or packaged into derivative collateral@babylonlabs_io 

Let’s imagine the mainnet hits a historic level crash, and Bitcoin network Gas fees get driven up to 500+ sat/vB by the liquidation wave. At that moment, if you want to urgently unbond and dump to save yourself, you don’t just have to endure the fixed 7-day “physical time” extension—your Unbonding transaction might also fail to get into the next block because the reserved Miner Fee from when you set it up wasn’t enough, leaving it stuck in the mempool.

Claiming “assets are absolutely safe” is one thing; the “actual realizable cost” of liquidity under extreme market conditions is another.#baby $BABY #ETH 

Next, I’ll be watching these indicators:
on-chain average retention time for Unbonding Output
the real de-peg/discount rate when the secondary market Liquid Staking Token (LST) faces large redemptions
self-custody safety claims for marketing purposes—because that’s not the same as “risk-free arbitrage” as traders talk about it.

content:

但很多人压根没翻过 BabylonGenesis 参数里的硬规定，BTC 解质押必须经过一个被称为 Unbonding Output 的 Taproot 交易脚本。官方文档写得清清楚楚，这个 Unbonding Output 强制绑定了一个 1008 个比特币区块的 Timelock（整整 7 天），而且内嵌了 Covenant 委员会的多签门限。

Look, teacher—let’s explain the RSI in a simple way.

This is a momentum indicator: it tells you whether the move is strong or whether it’s starting to get tired.
We use it to check alignment: if RSI is rising along with the price, the momentum is supportive. But if the price is rising while RSI is weakening, watch out for divergence.

The biggest mistake: selling just because RSI is above 70, or buying just because it’s below 30. You must look at the trend first.

Quick example: if the coin is in an uptrend and RSI drops back from 50 and then rises again, that’s a stronger continuation signal than randomly entering when RSI is around 30.

This time, the key angle: support and resistance matter more than excitement.

The indicator alone isn’t enough. Pair it with the trend, volume, support, and resistance—then your decision will be calmer and cleaner.

#ETH  From a Rented Room to Wulin Yihao: Four Lessons Worth $33.82 Million
In the summer of 2018, I lived in a rented apartment in Gongshu District, Hangzhou—15 square meters on the fifth floor with no elevator, so I climbed up on my own.
I had only 116 yuan left in my account. During the day I handed out flyers, at noon I carried plates, saved money, and at night I watched the K-line charts.
Eight years later, I was at Wulin Yihao, looking at an account balance of over 30 million.
It wasn’t luck—just four bloody lessons.
1. A sharp rise and sharp fall—there must be distribution
In the 2017 bull market, a so-called “shanzhai” coin surged 320% in ten days. I went all-in with 80,000.
The result: the third day it crashed 18%, and within a week I lost 60,000.
Later I understood: when it spikes up 30%+, then trades sideways for 3–5 days, and then drops 15% on increased volume— the market maker starts to retreat.
With this pattern, see it once and you short it once.
2. Consolidation at high levels isn’t an opportunity—it’s a trap
In 2019, I held a major coin and traded sideways for two months. I used leverage to add positions, but I ended up getting cut in half.
If consolidation lasts more than 20 days, turnover is below 2%, and price deviates from the 20-day moving average by 20% or more— it’s a distribution signal.
Once my system triggers this pattern, I immediately reduce my position.
3. Bottom signals—watch volume, not price
The March 12, 2020 crash happened, and I tried to bottom-fish LINK, only to get trapped.
Later I figured out: a real bottom is “low-volume consolidation + three consecutive days of gentle increased-volume small bullish candles.”
Last year when $BTC at 25,000 showed this pattern, I went all-in and bought at 25,000, then sold at 42,000. One trade netted 5.8 million.
5. Volume is the truth—position sizing decides life or death
If you can survive long enough, you earn the right to win.
I only trade with half positions and don’t use leverage.
Last year PEPE: I entered only after volume surged fivefold, and when the trend broke down, I immediately took profit.
Made 12x—avoided the brutal crashes and blow-off rips.
In the crypto market, it doesn’t matter who is the smartest. It only matters who can live through it.

The US, Japan, and South Korea working together to stabilize their currencies is, in essence, about concern over extreme volatility in the foreign-exchange market—volatility that ultimately transmits to the U.S. stock market through capital flows.

From what we’re seeing in the market, U.S. equities are in a critical period: the narrative driving the first phase of AI is gradually weakening, while the narrative for the second phase has not yet fully taken over.

The first phase relies on computing power, chips, and data centers to support valuations, while the market is waiting for second-phase stories such as autonomous driving, robotics, and AI applications to provide new growth expectations for high valuations.

The fact that this can hold up until today also owes a lot to “Huang Mao” continuously attracting investment, stimulating it, and helping keep market expectations steady before the midterm elections.

Over the past few years, excess investment has kept pushing capital-market valuations higher. Once the yen or the won shows sharp swings, global leveraged capital may be forced to unwind—thereby knocking into the U.S. stock market.

That’s why every intervention the US, Japan, and South Korea make in the FX market requires repeated coordination, especially involving Japan, since large-scale currency actions often cannot happen without communication with the United States.

After global capital, exchange rates, and the stock market become deeply intertwined, stabilizing currencies—somewhat in a sense—also means stabilizing the entire risk-asset market.

If Japan were to sell U.S. Treasuries to prop up the yen, both U.S. Treasuries and the U.S. stock market would inevitably collapse.

The US, Japan, and South Korea jointly intervening in the foreign-exchange market isn’t really something to be surprised by.

What’s going on
Guys, Ethereum developers are working on a new proposal called EIP-8361. In plain terms, they’re setting a red line for the network’s total staking issuance: it must not exceed 50%. Previously, as long as someone stakes their coins, the system continuously produces new coins as rewards. Now they want to step on the brakes and put a ceiling on total output. Market impact

但这种操作对币圈来说，就是实打实的砸盘抽血。上市公司清理加密资产，不管体量多大，情绪面上的打击非常直接，这意味着传统资本在压低加密资产的配置权重。

对市场的影响
短期来看，这绝对是利空。嘉楠带头卖币，其实反映了矿企和机构面临的资金压力。BTC和ETH盘面本来就比较脆，现在又来个上市公司清理库存，给多头浇了一盆冷水。资金正在从加密资产流出，回流传统股市。

中期来看，这种行业格局会让人警惕。如果连矿企都觉得囤币不如买自家股票，说明行业信心在动摇，其他持仓大户也可能跟风减仓。现在的恐慌情绪正在蔓延，多头想拉升阻力很大。

我的判断
讲真，看到这个消息我偏向看空。BTC现在在 $63,967.32 这个位置震荡，24h变动仅为0.19%，横盘缩量，本来就是在找方向。结果来了个矿企带头卖币的消息，多头士气受挫。我觉得短期内很难撑住，向下测试支撑位的概率大增。

ETH更是惨，24h微跌0.03%，报价 $1,867.74，本身就严重缺乏上涨动能，现在又有机构抛售预期。我的建议是最近别急着抄底，等这波抛压释放完再看。下方空间一旦打开，现货等跌透了再进场更安全。

One of the biggest lies in crypto is thinking your first profits prove you’re a good trader.

Imagine two people enter the market with $1,000.

One person buys during a strong bull market. Every coin he touches goes up 50%, 100%, even 300%. He starts believing he has mastered trading.

The second person enters during a bear market. He studies risk management, waits for confirmation, accepts small losses, and learns patience. For months, he barely makes any money.

A year later, the market changes.

The first trader keeps buying every pump because that’s all he has ever known. One bad cycle wipes out most of his profits.

While the second one finally gets a bull market. Now he has both opportunity and discipline. That’s when his account grows faster than everyone else’s.

Anyone can make money when everything is going up. Real traders are revealed when everything stops going up.

title: 还在只拿着2022年的山寨币吗？你可能正在错过真正的机会
subTitle:
如果你从2022年开始，一直只持有山寨币，那么过去几年里，标普500却走出了一轮强劲上涨行情。

拒绝分散投资，并不代表忠诚，有时候反而是在限制自己。长期只坚持一种投资方式，很容易让机会从身边溜走。

真正成熟的投资者，不会把全部希望押在单一市场上。加密货币、股票、现金和其他资产，都可以根据行情与风险承受能力进行合理配置。

不要一边等待山寨币奇迹般上涨，一边看着其他人通过更均衡的投资方式积累财富。

现在调整策略并不晚。与其执着于某一种资产，不如重新审视自己的仓位：

控制山寨币占比，避免过度集中；

保留一定现金，应对市场波动；

关注不同市场的机会；

定期复盘，而不是无限期死扛。

投资不是比谁更忠诚，而是比谁更懂得控制风险、抓住机会。

真正的升级，不是频繁交易，而是开始像一名成熟投资者那样思考。

本文仅为市场观点分享，不构成任何投资建议。加密资产波动较大，请根据自身情况谨慎决策。

Comparatively Real

Institutions have become the main force in the market, especially in the United States.

In a lifetime, it’s hard to encounter a financial market that has moved from adolescence to maturity. The crypto market has only existed for a little over ten years, while stock, bond, and forex markets have been developing for over a hundred years. What’s becoming increasingly clear now is that U.S. institutions, ETFs, market makers, and quantitative funds are gradually replacing early retail traders, becoming the true price-setters of the market.

Over the next decade, regulation, ETFs, stablecoin systems, and traditional capital may completely reshape market structure.

Cherish this moment of time.

In the course of a life, it’s rare to have the opportunity to personally witness a financial market grow up—from the savage, fast-growing “adolescence,” to maturity, ultimately becoming one of the most important forces in the global financial system.

Years from now, when we’re already old, perhaps we’ll be sitting on a balcony, reminiscing about all the endless late nights we pulled through when we were young—about the surges and crashes we witnessed, and the madness and despair we went through.

When you look back then, you’ll realize you once accompanied an era as it grew.

From experiments in the hands of geeks, to core assets at Wall Street institutions—from being overlooked and ignored, to influencing the flow of global capital.

We’re not just participating in an investment; we’re witnessing a piece of financial history.

When the market finally becomes truly mature, when arbitrage space gets smaller and volatility becomes gentler, those stories from the “youth era” will also eventually become the most worth-revisiting part of memory.

What’s truly scarce may not be any single bull market, but the entire process of an asset class moving from the margins to the mainstream. For many people, it’s difficult to encounter such an era even once in a lifetime.

比较真实

机构们已经成为市场主力，尤其美国机构。

人一辈子很难遇到一个金融市场从青春期走向成熟，加密市场诞生不过十几年，而股票、债券、外汇市场已经发展了上百年。现在越来越明显的一点是，美国机构、ETF、做市商、量化基金正在逐渐取代早期散户，成为市场真正的定价者。

未来十年，监管、ETF、稳定币体系、传统资本可能会彻底重塑市场结构。

珍惜当下这段时光。

人这一生，很难有机会亲眼见证一个金融市场从野蛮生长的青春期，逐渐走向成熟，最终成为全球金融体系最重要的力量之一。

若干年后，当我们已经老去，或许会坐在阳台上，回忆年轻时熬过的无数个深夜，看过的暴涨暴跌，经历过的疯狂与绝望。

那时候再回头看，会发现自己曾陪伴一个时代成长。

从极客手中的实验，到华尔街机构的核心资产，从无人问津，到影响全球资本流向。

我们不仅是在参与一场投资，更是在见证一段金融历史。

等到市场真正成熟，套利空间越来越小，波动越来越温和，那些属于青春时代的故事，也终将成为记忆里最值得回味的一部分。

真正稀缺的，可能不是某一个牛市，而是一个资产类别从边缘走向主流的全过程。对于很多人来说，一生很难碰上一次这样的时代。

Iran makes a major shift in attitude! Geopolitical tensions cool down—will BTC $64,076 take off?

💡 Positive factors📈: The easing of tensions in the Middle East reduces safe-haven sentiment, directly benefiting risk assets.

To put it simply: Iran is considering asking European countries to help clear mines in the Strait of Hormuz. Now BTC $64,076 (up 0.54% in 24h), ETH at $1,871 (up 0.37% in 24h)—the market is already pricing in the premium.

In one sentence

Iran signals openness to have Europe sweep mines; geopolitical tensions ease—risk assets like BTC and ETH look bullish in the short term.

What’s going on

Honestly, the Strait of Hormuz is too critical. Roughly one-fifth of the world’s oil has to pass through there. Previously, Iran placed mines there, causing chaos in the market: oil prices swung wildly, and safe-haven funds flooded into gold and U.S. Treasuries.

Now Iran unexpectedly signals openness, saying it is considering letting European countries help clear the mines. This is not a minor signal—it suggests Iran doesn’t want things to spiral into an unmanageable situation. With Europe participating in mine-sweeping, oil prices stabilize, geopolitical pressure eases, and the global macro environment gets a bit of breathing room too.

Market impact

In the short term, this is bullish for crypto. The logic is straightforward: geopolitical tensions cool → oil prices fall → inflation expectations improve → the probability of Fed rate cuts rises → risk assets benefit. BTC is already up 0.54% today to $64,076, and ETH is also up 0.37% to $1,871—showing smart money is already running ahead.

The medium-term impact is even more far-reaching. If tensions in the Middle East keep easing, institutional capital’s risk appetite should rise noticeably. The ETF funds that were previously on the sidelines are likely to flow back in.

My take

I’m bullish—short-term, just do it. BTC still has room to push higher from the $64,076 level. With the geopolitical tailwind stacked with a recovery in risk appetite, the target looks to be above $65,000. ETH is following up, but with weaker strength; the key is whether it can hold above $1,871 and break past $1,900 within 24 hours.

Brothers, remember this: trend reversals take time—don’t make an overconcentrated allocation in one go. Scale in, set stop-loss levels. This setup is meant for people with patience.

- Direction: Bullish 📈 Predicting an upside move
- Duration: BTC 12 hours / ETH 24 hours

Just now, Saudi Aramco’s CEO said they’re losing 100 million barrels of oil every week, and 2.6 billion barrels of crude oil have already been gone. Brent crude has jumped straight to $86.33 per barrel, up 3%.

The harshest part is that the traffic volume is now only 10% of what it was before the war. Even if they reopen tomorrow, rebuilding inventories will take 18 months. The energy market really can’t hold much longer.

Trump says this is Iran’s "last chance." Bessent says Hormuz could be "reopened tomorrow." But Iran’s stance is very tough—they absolutely won’t allow a second channel to be opened. Does this war still have to be fought?

The U.S. also looks pretty awkward here. Its long-range precision missiles are almost out. With inventories running low and resupply not keeping up, this war is a bit hard to fight.

From a crypto perspective, you might want to pay attention to safe-haven assets like $BTC and $ETH. When geopolitics is tense, capital often flows into hard assets.

SEC Commissioner Hester Peirce made headlines again today. In a CoinDesk podcast, she said she remains optimistic that the Clarity Act will pass—and even if it doesn’t, the SEC can still do a lot.

The weight of her remarks lies in the fact that Peirce is one of the most central figures inside the SEC overseeing crypto regulation. The crypto special task force she leads has been pushing rulemaking forward. She is scheduled to leave the SEC in November to become a professor at a university, so every sentence she says now carries the sense of making sure she leaves her message clearly before departing.

The Senate has very little time. This week leaves only four meeting days (August 4 to 7), and by mid-August it will enter recess. The bill has not yet been scheduled for a vote. Senator Jon Husted also came out today saying that the bipartisan versions are already ready—what’s left is to move the process forward.

At its core, the Clarity Act is about setting rules for digital assets: which fall under the SEC and which fall under the CFTC, how exchanges should register, and how developers can be shielded. Once this framework is in place, the compliance paths for \$BTC  and \$ETH  will become much clearer. But legislation is not guaranteed just because the process reaches a certain stage—you still have to see how the Senate ultimately votes.

After I repaid the Aave v4 loan on TBV’s testnet last night, I kept refreshing the page several times: the debt was cleared—so why hadn’t the BTC come back to my wallet? In that moment, I almost translated “trustless” as “please wait.” Later, by re-reading the whitepaper alongside the transaction status, I realized I’d mixed up two different clocks.

The first clock is on the Aave side: it confirms the debt, the collateral ratio, and the repayment status. The second clock is on the Bitcoin side: it waits for external state proof to enter the predefined redemption path, and then completes the challenge window.

TBV’s @babylonlabs_io  isn’t forcing these two steps into the same chain. Instead, it keeps native BTC in its own independent UTXO. Applications can decide whether your position meets the redemption condition, but they can’t, like custodial platforms, arbitrarily decide on the spot with something like “withdrawals are paused today.”

That also helped me understand the weight of “exit safety” in the whitepaper: it’s not about who gets instant settlement—it’s about who holds the final veto power. In the wrapped-BTC model, I receive an on-chain certificate issued by the custodian, and redemption depends on whether the counterparty is online and cooperative. In TBV, the financial rules must be satisfied—but the underlying BTC doesn’t have to be transferred first into someone else’s funds pool.

The most practical feedback I’ve gotten from the public testnet is to split the page into four states: “debt cleared—proof generation in progress—challenge period countdown—BTC redeemed.” Right now, a single “processing” label makes it too easy to assume things are stuck, and even makes people want to take it out on the router.

What truly attracts me to TBV isn’t faster execution—it’s separating borrowing state from asset control: rules can govern my position, but others can’t conveniently grab control of my exit. $BABY  #baby  #BTC #ETH

translatedData.content:
Ethereum has yet another new proposal🔥

EIP-8361 has officially been released, and the core idea is simple: use “burning” to fight inflation.

The proposal introduces a dynamic burning mechanism:
▸ When the staking ratio is low, in each epoch a portion is deducted from validator block rewards and burned
▸ When the staking ratio exceeds the 50% threshold, the burn rate is ramped directly up to 100%, meaning all block rewards are burned
▸ The final cut-off point is determined by market game theory, but with a hard constraint: it must be strictly less than 50%

What does this mean?

Once Ethereum’s total staked amount approaches half, the validator earnings model will change fundamentally—rewards will no longer be “sent out,” but instead be reclaimed at the protocol level.

Supporters believe this is a powerful tool for ETH to move toward deflation;
critics are concerned: with a high staking ratio, 100% burning could severely dampen the enthusiasm of large validators, triggering a reversal toward centralization in staking.

At the moment, the proposal is still in the early discussion phase. Whether it will ultimately be included in Ethereum’s upgrade roadmap depends on the outcome of the community and core developers’ debate.

What do you think about EIP-8361? A new piece of ammunition for the deflationary narrative, or Pandora’s box for staking economics? Let’s discuss in the comments 👇

content:
以太坊又有新提案了🔥

EIP-8361 正式发布，核心思路很简单：用"销毁"来对抗通胀。

提案设计了一套动态销毁机制：
▸ 质押率较低时，每个 epoch 从验证者区块奖励中扣除并销毁一部分
▸ 质押率超过 50% 阈值时，销毁率直接拉满到 100%，相当于区块奖励全部烧毁
▸ 最终的停发临界点由市场博弈决定，但硬性约束：必须严格小于 50%

这意味着什么？

一旦以太坊总质押量逼近半数，验证者收益模型将发生根本性变化——奖励不再"发出去"，而是被协议层面回收。

支持者认为这是 ETH 走向通缩的有力工具；
质疑者则担忧：高质押率下 100% 销毁会严重打击大额验证者的积极性，引发 staking 中心化逆转。

目前该提案处于早期讨论阶段，最终能否纳入以太坊升级路线图，还需看社区与核心开发者的博弈结果。

EIP-8361 is here—the goal is to “fat-trim” Ethereum.

Simply put, this proposal wants to deduct a portion of validators’ block rewards to be directly burned in every epoch. Once the staking ratio reaches 50%, the burn rate would be cranked up to 100%—meaning all block rewards are burned. The proposal also says that the final, specific halting/burning proportion would be determined by market forces, but the cap is strictly less than 50%.

The logic is straightforward: the more people stake, the more rewards get burned, thereby putting a lid on the inflation curve.

An interesting game-theory angle here is this: when the burn rate hits 100%, validators only earn transaction fees + MEV. This structure would push large holders to think, “Stake or leave and take the money.” For the long-term supply/demand model of $ETH , this is a rewrite.

Worth tracking: the EIP number is only up to 8361, which suggests the Ethereum community’s discussion of a “deflation mechanism” is still in a very early stage, and it won’t affect the mainnet in the short term.

Look, teacher—let’s explain Bollinger Bands simply.

Bollinger Bands show whether the price has moved far from its average or if it’s still within a normal range.
We use them to spot compression inside the bands, and then a potential breakout with volume could bring a solid move.

The biggest mistake: selling at the upper band in a strong uptrend. The price can ride the band for a long time.

Quick example: if the bands are tight and the price breaks with volume, we watch for a retest instead of getting impatient.

This time’s follow-up angle: split the trade into stages if you’re going to continue.

The indicator alone isn’t enough. Pair it with the trend, volume, support, and resistance—then the decision becomes calmer and cleaner.

Look, teach, let’s explain ATR simply.

ATR measures currency volatility, and that’s very important before setting a stop-loss.
We use it so that when volatility increases, your stop-loss and the distance between your targets are calculated calmly.

The biggest mistake: placing a very tight stop on a highly volatile coin, so you get stopped out before the normal move.

Quick example: if ATR is high, wait for a clearer zone and reduce the position size instead of increasing risk.

That’s the follow-up angle this time: if the picture isn’t clear, skipping the opportunity is a respectable decision.

An indicator alone isn’t enough. Link it with the trend, volume, support, and resistance, and then the decision becomes calmer and cleaner.

Do follow-up so you get every update. Educational content, not financial advice.
